summary: Renamed products.type to kind with a closed product|service domain, added the default payment/config block plus the sales_ops_product_funcao_costs child table, and wired POST/PATCH/GET plus /bootstrap - backend only.
migration: 0013_produtos_servicos_defaults.sql, journal idx 13 (newest before it was idx 12 / 0012_sales_ops_funcoes, confirmed by re-reading _journal.json)
data_audit: Ran `SELECT count(*) AS total_products, count(*) FILTER (WHERE open_price) AS open_price_rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE open_price AND (setup_brl <> 0 OR monthly_brl <> 0)) AS would_be_altered FROM sales_ops_products;` plus `SELECT id, name, setup_brl, monthly_brl FROM sales_ops_products WHERE open_price AND (setup_brl <> 0 OR monthly_brl <> 0);` and `SELECT DISTINCT type FROM sales_ops_products;` against the local Docker test DB (container 06--product--fxl-sales-db-1, port 5006, db fxl_sales) BEFORE applying the migration. Result: total_products=0, open_price_rows=0, would_be_altered=0, zero rows returned by the detail query, zero distinct type values. So NO real data would be altered locally - the local test DB is empty of products because the integration suites clean up after themselves. IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR THE HUMAN: this audit therefore proves nothing about staging or production, which I deliberately did not touch (apps/api/.env DATABASE_URL points at staging, and `db:migrate` reads DATABASE_URL, so I never ran it - the local DB was migrated by the integration suite's globalSetup via TEST_MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL). The same SELECT MUST be re-run against staging and production before 0013 is applied there, and any non-zero `would_be_altered` count escalated rather than worked around, because the zeroing UPDATE is the one irreversible step in this batch.

suite: lint=0 type-check=0 test=0 integration=0 build=0 api=27/283 integration=18/88 (baseline was api 24/248, integration 16/73, web 30/210 and shared-utils 1/17 - web and shared-utils are unchanged at 30/210 and 1/17)
drizzle_drift: none - `npx drizzle-kit generate` reports 'No schema changes, nothing to migrate' after the final edits
statement_order_checked: Checked, and no reordering was needed for the FK hazard: this slice's composite FK targets sales_ops_funcoes_org_id_id_idx, which migration 0012 already created, so drizzle-kit could not emit it out of order. What DID need hand-reordering is the hazard the plan predicted: drizzle-kit emitted all six `ADD CONSTRAINT ... CHECK` statements inside the DDL block, above the backfill. I moved every one of them below the two backfill UPDATEs. Also deleted nothing spurious - drizzle-kit did not re-emit sales_ops_funcoes_org_id_id_idx (test 21 pins that). No ON CONFLICT upsert is written anywhere in this slice, so the 23505 hazard does not apply.
red_confirmed: Wrote the three unit oracle files, then reverted apps/api/src/db/schema.ts, service.ts, routes.ts and drizzle/meta/_journal.json to HEAD and moved 0013_produtos_servicos_defaults.sql aside. All 31 new unit tests went Red for the right reasons: produtos-servicos-contract.test.ts (12) and default-payment-plan.test.ts (9) failed on missing exports (UpdateProductSchema, resolveProductKind, materializeDefaultPaymentPlan, ProductPaymentDefaults) and on ProductSchema still accepting `type`/independent `openPrice`; produtos-servicos-migration.test.ts (10) failed on 'missing migration: drizzle/0013_produtos_servicos_defaults.sql' and on the journal having no idx 13. Restored via `git apply` of the saved patch and confirmed schema.ts, service.ts and the migration SQL are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-revert copies with `diff`.
mutations_observed: Nine mutations, each applied then reverted with a byte-identity `diff` check. (1) kind/openPrice projection: changed createProduct's `openPrice: kind === 'service'` to `openPrice: data.openPrice ?? false` -> 8 of 9 integration tests Red. (2) orgId filter on the cost select: deleted `eq(salesOpsProductFuncaoCosts.orgId, orgId)` -> ONLY 'keeps cost rows out of another org even over an admin connection' went Red; all eight app-role tests stayed green, reproducing slice 05's finding exactly. (3) unknown_funcao pre-check: replaced the `return { ok: false, reason: 'unknown_funcao' }` with a no-op -> 'rejects a funcao id owned by another org' Red. (4) merged-row invariant: removed the `UpdateProductSchema.safeParse(kindMerged)` guard -> 'a servico cannot be given a fixed own value through PATCH' Red. (5) full-replace cost set: deleted the DELETE in replaceProductFuncaoCosts so the set merged -> 'funcao cost defaults round-trip' Red. (6) duplicate_funcao_cost: changed the issue message -> 'rejects duplicate funcaoId rows' Red. (7) migration RENAME: replaced `RENAME COLUMN "type" TO "kind"` with DROP COLUMN + ADD COLUMN, i.e. exactly what a wrong db:generate prompt answer emits -> 'renames type to kind ...' Red. (8) backfill rule: inverted the CASE to `WHEN open_price THEN 'product' ELSE 'service'` -> 'backfills kind from open_price for real rows' and 'leaves the backfilled table able to take the three post-backfill CHECK constraints' Red. (9) data-safety UPDATE: deleted the `SET setup_brl = 0, monthly_brl = 0 WHERE open_price` statement -> 2 unit + 5 integration replay tests Red. Plus a live-DB mutation: dropped sales_ops_products_kind_check, kind_open_price_check, service_no_fixed_value_check and sales_ops_product_funcao_costs_org_funcao_fk from the test database -> 5 integration tests Red, proving the DB-level oracles are not tautologies; all four constraints were re-added and verified present via pg_constraint.
orgid_filters_proven: Deleted `eq(salesOpsProductFuncaoCosts.orgId, orgId)` from selectProductFuncaoCosts (both the per-product and whole-org branches). Under the app role every existing test stayed GREEN, because FORCE RLS on sales_ops_product_funcao_costs silently covered the missing filter. The new test 'keeps cost rows out of another org even over an admin connection' drives createProduct / listProducts / listProductFuncaoCosts / getSalesOpsSnapshot / updateProduct over a drizzle instance built on a postgres client with connection option app.fxl_admin='true' - the admin policy exposes every org, so the missing filter surfaces immediately, and that test went Red. It carries positive controls in both directions (the owning org still reads its row and can still PATCH it). Filter restored and verified byte-identical.
openprice_alias_still_works: Four independent proofs. (1) Unit: 'still accepts the exact payload master product dialog sends' parses a payload carrying the now-removed `type: 'SaaS'`, `openPrice: true`, no `kind`, and a populated deprecated `providers` array; it asserts resolveProductKind returns 'service', that `type` is STRIPPED rather than rejected (Zod objects default to strip), and that providers round-trips unchanged. (2) Unit: 'accepts the legacy openPrice alias and maps it to kind service' plus 'rejects a kind and openPrice contradiction' with agreeing-pair positive controls. (3) Route: new routes.test.ts case 'accepts the deprecated openPrice alias on the create payload' asserts POST /products returns 201 and forwards openPrice. (4) Integration: 'openPrice stays equal to kind service in the database' creates a product through the alias only and asserts kind='service' / open_price=true, then PATCHes with `{ openPrice: false }` and asserts kind flips to 'product'. apps/web is untouched and its suite is unchanged at 30 files / 210 tests.
api_contract_matches_plan: Matches, with one additive extension and one forced test-side reading. ADDITIVE: updateProduct can also return the sentinel INVALID_PRODUCT_ENTRADA_VALUE, which PATCH /products/:id maps to 400 { error: 'validation_error', reason: 'entrada_mode_value_mismatch' }. Without it, `PATCH { defaultEntradaPct: 50 }` against a row whose stored mode is 'none' is invisible to the partial schema and would hit sales_ops_products_default_entrada_mode_check as an unhandled 23514, i.e. an HTTP 500 - the same class of defect slice 05 shipped. INVALID_PRODUCT_KIND_VALUE keeps the plan's exact value and its exact 400/service_cannot_have_fixed_value mapping. FORCED READING: the plan's tests 24-25 say 'the FIRST statement containing ADD CONSTRAINT', but the plan's own SQL layout puts the new child table's two foreign keys (also ADD CONSTRAINT statements) in the DDL block ABOVE the backfill, so a literal 'first' makes the window empty. Both tests therefore use 'the first ADD CONSTRAINT AFTER the set_config', which is the only self-consistent reading, and the replay helper hard-asserts the resulting slice is exactly 3 statements. Everything else - ProductRow / ProductFuncaoCostRow shapes, the flat productFuncaoCosts key on GET /products, POST, PATCH and /bootstrap, the { product, productFuncaoCosts } response bodies, the unknown_area / unknown_funcao reason codes, materializeDefaultPaymentPlan's signature and all seven algorithm steps, and the Default config shape Zod block - is as written, so slices 08, 10 and 12 are unaffected.
tests_changed: Five existing files, all mechanical. apps/api/src/domains/sales-ops/__tests__/areas-contract.test.ts: `ProductSchema.partial()` no longer exists (ProductSchema is now a ZodEffects), so it asserts through UpdateProductSchema. apps/api/src/domains/sales-ops/__tests__/routes.test.ts: routes now call resolveProductRefs instead of getArea, so the mock and the unknown_area case were retargeted; productResult became the { product, productFuncaoCosts } shape; added four new cases (unknown_funcao, response body, openPrice alias, kind/openPrice contradiction). apps/api/test/rls/product-commission-contract.test.ts and apps/api/test/rls/proposal-write.test.ts: destructure `{ product }` out of createProduct/updateProduct's new return shape. No assertion was weakened; the only relaxation is inside the NEW round-trip test, where a `toEqual([...])` on cost rows became `toHaveLength(2)` + `arrayContaining` PLUS an explicit `map(funcaoId) === [a, b].sort()` assertion, because rows come back ordered by (productId, funcaoId) and the fixture uuids sort non-deterministically - that mis-assertion actually failed on the first full integration run and the fix pins the documented ordering more precisely than the original did.
notes: 1) DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN'S files_modified, on the orchestrator's explicit instruction: the plan lists nine apps/web files (types.ts, SalesOpsApp.tsx and seven test fixtures) as a forced mechanical rename, and its Risk 16 claims type-check cannot stay green without them. That claim is wrong, and I verified it: apps/web/src/sales-ops/types.ts is a HAND-WRITTEN mirror, not generated from the API, so renaming the API column does not touch web typing at all. lint, type-check, build and the full web suite (30 files / 210 tests) are all green with apps/web byte-untouched. The only runtime consequence is SalesOpsApp.tsx:4343 `productType: product?.type ?? 'SaaS'`, which now always takes the 'SaaS' fallback - and SaleItemSchema strips that field while the server derives product_type_snapshot from `kind`, so there is zero behavioural change. Slice 10 should still do the rename for honesty. 2) SPEC EDGE FOUND, pinned not fixed: defaultRemainingInstallments is bounded at 120 and the entrada row sits ON TOP of it, so a product configured with an entrada plus 120 parcelas generates 121 installments, one more than CreateSaleSchema's `installments: max(120)` accepts. I did NOT clamp it, because clamping would make slice 11's web mirror diverge from the shipped reference implementation. The test 'documents the one template that overflows the 120-row API ceiling' pins the behaviour, and the two boundary vectors (120 + no entrada, 119 + entrada) are exercised as positive controls. Slice 10's editor should cap the pair. 3) db:generate PROMPTS INTERACTIVELY on the rename and the Bash harness runs commands with stdin closed, so it hangs. I got a correct file WITHOUT answering the prompt by generating twice: pass A with `type` and `kind` both present (pure addition, no prompt), pass B with `type` removed (pure drop, no prompt). Drizzle snapshots record only the final schema state, so pass B's snapshot IS the correct 0013 snapshot; I renamed it, repointed its prevId at 0012's id, deleted the 0014 artifacts and the stray journal entry, and hand-wrote the SQL as a RENAME. `db:generate` then reports no drift, and the integration suite replays the shipped SQL against Postgres. Worth recording for the next agent that has to rename a column. 4) Postgres truncates the drizzle-generated FK name sales_ops_product_funcao_costs_product_id_sales_ops_products_id_fk to 63 chars on apply (a NOTICE, not an error); harmless, but the DB name differs from the snapshot name. 5) `pnpm --filter @fxl-sales/api db:migrate` reads DATABASE_URL, which apps/api/.env points at STAGING, so I never ran it. The local test DB was migrated by the integration suite's globalSetup through TEST_MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL. Anyone following the plan's Green step 7 literally would migrate staging by accident. 6) The plan's Refactor item about a shared numeric helper landed as productNumericPatch + numericColumn, and the `...data` spread in createProduct was replaced by an explicit PRODUCT_PLAIN_COLUMNS allow-list, which additionally makes it structurally impossible for a request body to smuggle orgId/id/createdAt into a product write. 7) The plan's getFuncoesByIds exists and resolvePersonFuncoes was refactored onto the same selectFuncoesByIds helper, so there is one id-verification query, not two copies.
